unresolved_added: Equation 4-11 hard-codes x1, c2, and x2 inside a claimed general k-species equation.
Equation 5-23 prints f(T)=mu1*T+mu2 although its context and Figure 5 require MT_k=mu1*ER_k+mu2.
Equation 5-24 prints an inconsistent equality chain between d eta_D/dt, f(T), and the biomass sum.
The metric paragraph says higher decomposition-speed variance means greater stability, opposite to the later lower-variance conclusions.
Figure 6 repeats Multiple Fungal Ecosystem roles in all four panel captions rather than distinguishing the priority/single case.
The temperature law is fitted from only three selected coefficients and is used beyond a demonstrated predictive test.
The low r=0.3255 ER-MT association is described as if ER nearly determines moisture tolerance.
Five weather categories are scenario transfers, not field validation of fungal biomass or decomposition.
Figure 9's coexistence/priority boundary panel lacks readable numeric axes and scale needed to reproduce the boundary.
Biodiversity is conceptual; richness, composition-balanced subsets, and a diversity optimum are not directly simulated.
The code uses the ER-MT intercept 2.5953 while the prose and equation state 2.96.
The code multiplies stored biomass plots and decomposition speed by an unexplained factor 1.5.
The printed code omits the random pulse and most competition, climate, and sensitivity loops claimed by the figures.
Below the 5 mm survival threshold, negative capacity and competition terms remain active instead of simply stopping growth.
The printed competition update creates squared focal-biomass dependence through an outer x and an inner x_self*x_other term.
The tuned x0 and derived xm are assessed against the same curve used to select x0.
